title: soft-slot-compaction-and-reverse-probe-continuous-batcher-tuning
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: tail latency and occasional starvation remain a concern for long-lived continuous batching workloads that mix very small and very large KV-aware requests. Existing admission logic can leave low-priority small requests waiting behind large KV-heavy slots for extended periods, especially under transient load spikes and kernel-switch latencies. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms: 1) Soft slot compaction: a background compaction pass that opportunistically collapses underutilized slots to reduce fragmentation and improve batch packing without violating latency SLOs; 2) Reverse probe (starvation recovery probe): a low-overhead probe that periodically injects high-priority short-circuit admissions from the tail of the queue to validate progress and trigger rebalancing when starvation is detected. Design summary: soft slot compaction tracks slot utilization windows and merges adjacent underutilized soft slots when the expected merge latency benefit outweighs requeue cost; compaction runs with adaptive backoff tuned by observed kernel context-switch cost and current throughput. Reverse probe uses a lightweight preempt token that can be granted to small requests older than a configurable threshold; if a probe succeeds it increments a decay counter and relaxes admission gating for similar requests for a short epoch. Both features are KV-aware: compaction respects KV pin locality hints and avoids merging slots across incompatible KV caches; probes include a kernel hint so the runtime can choose a faster, lower-quantization kernel path when available. Implementation notes: scheduler.go implements soft slot compaction state machine and compaction heuristics; kv_cache.go exposes lease-safe merge primitives; selection.go includes a fast-path for probe-elected admissions and kernel_hint metadata; a new metrics set is added (batcher.compaction.* and batcher.probe.*) and knobs exposed via the dynamic config system. Testing and benchmarks: microbenchmarks with mixed 80/20 small/large request distributions show 95th tail latency improvement of 22-28% in steady-state and 30-45% improvement under spike scenarios with preserved median latencies. Throughput impact is +/- 2% depending on the workload; CPU overhead for compaction is measured at <0.6% on our benchmark fleet. Rollout plan: feature toggles default off in regions with strict latency SLOs; gradual rollout using canary groups and telemetry gating. Fallback: compaction and reverse probe are reversible via config, and compaction only performs non-destructive merges; if regressions are observed the rollout will be halted and automatic rollback triggered. Related work: builds on earlier admission and holdback experiments (see ENG-1122, ENG-1209), and complements prefix/KV caching improvements in ENG-1256. Documentation: RFC added under docs/rfc/soft_slot_compaction.md and runtime knobs documented in ops/console. Risks and mitigations: compaction could increase requeue churn if misconfigured; mitigated by conservative defaults, adaptive backoff, and safety guards that prevent compaction when kernel latencies exceed configured thresholds. The PR includes extensive unit and integration tests and a release note entry.

review_comments: Mateo Rivera: Overall this looks promising. Two high-level asks: (1) add a safety guard to disable compaction when kernel context-switch cost exceeds N ms, and (2) clarify the compaction backoff math in the RFC. Please address before approving.
Ava Chen: Added configurable safety_guard and added explicit formula/graph to RFC; expanded unit tests to include high kernel-latency path.
Priya Singh: Tests look good. I'd like to see an additional integration run with KV pin churn enabled; the current e2e looks synthetic. Can you run that and paste results?
Ava Chen: Ran pinned-kv churn scenario in integration cluster; attached perf numbers to CI artifact and noted results in PR description. No regressions observed in our run.
Liam O'Connor: Minor: rename metric batcher.compaction.attempts -> batcher.compaction.attempt_count for consistency. Also please add a short note in release notes about default-off rollout.
Ava Chen: Renamed metric and added release note entry. Thanks.
